newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 20.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 20.0 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 20.0 percent of its average daily volume of 509.0 million shares, or 101.7 million shares, for the week of March 17-21.
Program trading accounted for an average of 13.6 percent of average daily volume of 489.6 million shares for the week of March 10-14.
Of the average 101.7 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 55.0 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 46.7 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 146.8 million shares a day during the week of March 17-21.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, NatWest, Susquehanna Brokerage Services and Goldman Sachs executed most of its program activity for customers.
Morgan Stanley executed most of its program activity as principal for its own account.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 65.2 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 33.0 percent of program volume from March 17-21.

Between March 17 and March 21, 32.9 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 0.7 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, the exchange said.
